DEP is seeking up to two (2) qualified vendors to provide Environmental Assessment and Professional Engineering Services, under a “Demand Services Contract” to support various tasks undertaken by the Stream Management Program (SMP) in the protection of water quality in the Catskill and Delaware Districts of the NYC Water Supply Watershed. Some of these professional services will be required on short notice to enable DEP to effectively respond in a timely manner to a broad range of local and regional water quality issues and concerns related to both planned and unplanned stream management activities. This contract shall not be limited to a specific project or projects but shall allow the SMP to assign the consultant specific tasks on an as-needed basis. Specific water quality related tasks may include: stream channel and floodplain restoration design, construction inspection and monitoring; hydrology, hydraulics and sediment transport modeling and analysis; elevation surveys of ground and water surfaces to support hydraulic and geomorphic analyses for stream management planning and stream restoration design and construction; geotechnical hillslope analysis adjacent to watercourses; engineering review of stream projects, including NYS Article 15 Stream Disturbance Permit application reviews and associated site assessment and characterization; mapping of riparian vegetation and land cover; mapping of streambanks with high risk of erosion (erosion hazard areas); statistical analysis of stream monitoring data to relate rates of change of bed, banks and floodplain to flow regime, channel morphology, substrate and vegetation; and public outreach to organizations, environmental groups, and other technically-oriented interest groups, related to the preceding tasks.

rows.description: Customer Relationship Management Upgrade Master Agreement for Capital Purchase. New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) is currently seeking to facilitate the upgrade of several division-specific primary applications from the on-prem Microsoft Dynamics Customer Relationship Management version to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Power Platform, to ensure continued support, cost savings in terms of infrastructure, maintenance, and upgrades, as well as compliance from a security standpoint. These applications play a pivotal role within the agency's new cloud-based Customer Relationship Management Back-office system (Business Automation) and Business Portal, designed to offer a comprehensive suite of online services to both DCWP clients and divisional staff.

CRO-655CM DEP is seeking a vendor to perform On Call Construction Management Services for Projects throughout the Upstate Watershed for Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Geotechnical and Structural Engineering projects.

DEP is seeking a Contractor for standard services to maintain and repair City-owned stormwater best management practices (BMPs) in the East of Hudson watershed. These BMPs include services such as landscaping, diving services and vegetation control. These facilities are critical to protecting water quality and complying with our Filtration Avoidance Determination.

DEP is seeking up to two (2) qualified vendors to provide Environmental Assessment and Professional Engineering Services, under a “Demand Services Contract” to support various tasks undertaken by the Stream Management Program (SMP) in the protection of water quality in the Catskill and Delaware Districts of the New York City Water Supply Watershed. Some of these professional services will be required on short notice to enable DEP to effectively respond in a timely manner to a broad range of local and regional water quality issues and concerns related to both planned and unplanned stream management activities. This contract shall not be limited to a specific project or projects but shall allow the SMP to assign the consultant specific tasks on an as-needed basis. Specific water quality related tasks may include: stream channel and floodplain restoration design, construction inspection and monitoring; hydrology, hydraulics and sediment transport modeling and analysis; elevation surveys of ground and water surfaces to support hydraulic and geomorphic analyses for stream management planning and stream restoration design and construction; geotechnical hillslope analysis adjacent to watercourses; engineering review of stream projects, including NYS Article 15 Stream Disturbance Permit application reviews and associated site assessment and characterization; mapping of riparian vegetation and land cover; mapping of streambanks with high risk of erosion (erosion hazard areas); statistical analysis of stream monitoring data to relate rates of change of bed, banks and floodplain to flow regime, channel morphology, substrate and vegetation; and public outreach to organizations, environmental groups, and other technically-oriented interest groups, related to the preceding tasks.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to provide all necessary labor, parts, materials and equipment for the scheduled preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, and as-needed repair of fire alarm system and fire suppression system equipment at New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection Bureau of Water Supply's Croton Filtration Plant in Bronx, NY.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to provide all necessary labor, parts, materials and equipment for the scheduled preventive maintenance and as-needed repair of various pumps at multiple New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection Bureau of Water Supply locations.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to provide all necessary labor, parts, materials and equipment for the scheduled preventive maintenance and as-needed repair of Chemical pumps at multiple New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection Bureau of Water Supply locations.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to provide diving services for underwater investigation and/or repairs at multiple DEP Bureau of Water Supply locations. The diving services include underwater investigation and/or repairs to under water structures, sluice gates, valves, pipes, concrete, tanks, silt curtains and aqueducts, and associated work at locations in the Bronx, Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess, Delaware, Ulster, Greene, Schoharie and Sullivan Counties. Underwater repairs may include: installation of piping or new equipment, under water cutting, patching, cement work or grouting of joints, leaks, cracks and fissures, and removal of organic growth.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to perform Chemical Bulk Storage Tank Cleaning and Inspections at multiple DEP Bureau of Water Supply facilities in the Bronx, Westchester, Putnam, Ulster, and Orange Counties. The tanks are critical to the operation of the facilities and require periodic cleaning to limit deficiencies.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to perform Tank Repair at multiple DEP Bureau of Water Supply facilities. The tanks are critical to the operation of the facilities and may require repairs and refurbishment.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a contract to upgrade Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Equipment, Software, Networks and Security. The SCADA system enables control of the water treatment system and is essential to the provision of drinking water. The technology of the current system is out of date and requires updates.

New York City Department of Enviornmental Protection is seeking a vendor to contract for Standard Services to Supply & Deliver Sulfuric Acid chemical 78% and 93% Solution. The 78% Solution Sulfuric Acid is needed at the Catskill Aqueduct to help remove and maintain the removal of a biofilm that has developed on the aqueduct walls. The 93% Solution Sulfuric Acid is needed at the Croton Filtration Plant to treat the taste and odor issue related to less than optimal water quality attributes of the New Croton system due to the presence of specific algae.

Point Blank Ballistic Vests - The Department of Homeless Services (DHS) Police are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of DHS clients, staff, and visitors. In performing their duties, DHS Peace Officers are exposed to several injuries as a result of detaining clients which may include stabbing or slashing with sharp objects such as knives, needles, broken glass bottles, and “shives.” DHS Officers may be threatened with guns and hit with various types of weapons while performing their jobs. The ballistic vests requested are utilized to absorb the impact from these attacks. The vests will minimize injury to DHS Police Officers and, therefore, minimize potential leave resulting from these injuries.

Digital Memo Book - DHS is seeking to transition from traditional, handwritten memo books to a digital eMemo Book solution. This solution consists of an integrated mobile application, hardware device combination, and a secure centralized database. It will allow Peace Officers to record field notes efficiently, eliminating the administrative burden and inefficiencies of physical, paper-based logs. The program's requirements are as follows: 1. Integration -must allow current processes and forms to be integrated; 2. Security & Defensibility - must be secure; 3. Searchability - must be able to search using various options/terms such as name of supervising officer, incident/case #, arresting officer name, etc.; 4. Compliance - must comply with governing laws/policies; 5. Professional services to assist with maintenance and troubleshooting

X-ray Machines - DHS Peace Officers are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of DHS clients, staff, and visitors. X-ray machines use low-dose penetrating rays to quickly determine organic, inorganic, metallic, or non-metallic items in your baggage kept under any body cavity or cloth. During the screening process, these machines identify dangerous objects by looking at their atomic numbers and mass densities. The device limits the need for physical searches of clients, staff, and visitors' personal belongings. These devices generally have an 8 to 10-year life span. Having non-functional machines compromises the security staff and our clients.

Magnetometers/Walk Through Metal Detectors (WTMD) - DHS Peace Officers are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of DHS clients, staff, and visitors. WTMD's use an electromagnetic field to detect metal objects, such as handguns and sharp objects. This device limits the need for physical searches with clients, staff, and visitors. These devices generally have a lifespan of 8 to 10 years. Having non-functional machines compromises the security staff and our clients.
